claim: spec/emit/arch_changeset_builder.md's "Interface" section (line 17): "The builder is set up once per run from four values that do not change while it runs — the spec graph, the journal fold, the git HEAD SHA and the proposal ref — and is then handed exactly one impact report." This omits Registration as one of the values ChangesetBuilder is set up from.
authoritative_source: emit/builder.go's Builder doc comment and struct (lines 9-25): "Builder is set up once per run from the five values that do not change while it runs — SpecGraph, Fold, Registration, GitHead, Proposal". Registration gates epic synthesis (`synthesizeEpic := !hasExistingEpic && b.Registration.OK`, emit/builder.go:40) and is threaded to Labeler.LabelFor and Resolver. arch_resolver.md:102 already carries the equivalent correction ("Resolver is set up with four things — the spec graph, the journal fold, the run's registration, …"), added by e7f20ab (drift-fix) alongside arch_emit_command.md, flow_emit.md and test_changeset_builder.md — arch_changeset_builder.md's own Interface section is the one leaf that sentence never reached.
evidence: arch_changeset_builder.md line 17 is the only place this leaf states the component's setup interface, and it undercounts by one: it lists spec graph, journal fold, git HEAD SHA and proposal ref, but not Registration, even though the leaf's own body already documents Registration's role in the label scheme ("Every label is `spex:<eid>` of the op's referent journal event") and the sibling leaves (arch_resolver.md, arch_emit_command.md, flow_emit.md, test_changeset_builder.md) were all updated to name Registration as a Builder input when the `spex:<eid>` label scheme landed (389b6c7, a56a928). No code change is implicated — hasExistingEpic and synthesizeEpic in emit/builder.go already read b.Registration correctly; only this leaf's prose is stale.
proposed_fix: Change arch_changeset_builder.md:17 to name five values instead of four: "The builder is set up once per run from five values that do not change while it runs — the spec graph, the journal fold, the run's registration, the git HEAD SHA and the proposal ref — and is then handed exactly one impact report."
